items.headline: Governor Ron DeSantis announces $60 million in cancer innovation awards and opens $70 million application cycle
items.summary: Florida announced $60 million in awards through the 2025-26 Florida Cancer Innovation Fund and opened the 2026-27 application cycle with $70 million available for new awards.
items.source: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida

items.headline: Florida regulators approve additional power for JEA's $1.57 billion, 675-megawatt natural-gas plant
items.summary: The Florida Public Service Commission approved JEA's need for additional power to support construction of a combined-cycle plant at the former St. Johns River Power Park site. Officials said the approval keeps the project on schedule to begin operations in 2031.

items.headline: SwRI develops dynamic framework to better predict wildfires
items.summary: Southwest Research Institute announced a framework for early wildfire detection that combines datasets, remote sensing and real-time modeling. The institute said the tool can identify risk factors up to 30 days before a wildfire outbreak.

items.headline: NYC Health Department detects first person with West Nile virus in 2026
items.summary: New York City's Health Department reported the first city resident with West Nile virus this year. The department said it intensified mosquito surveillance and expanded control efforts after virus-positive mosquitoes were detected across all five boroughs.
items.source: New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

items.headline: Appellate court reverses judgment in NYCERS accidental-disability retirement case
items.summary: New York's Appellate Division, Second Department reversed a lower-court judgment and dismissed a petition challenging the New York City Employees' Retirement System's denial of accidental-disability retirement benefits. The court held that NYCERS had a rational basis for its determination.
items.entityName: New York City Employees' Retirement System
items.source: New York State Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department

items.headline: Summit County advises Medicaid clients about possible work requirement
items.summary: Summit County reported that the Ohio Department of Medicaid is mailing notices to some Group VIII Medicaid enrollees about federal work requirements scheduled to begin January 1, 2027. The release says affected residents may need to document 80 hours of approved activities each month and renew coverage every six months.

items.headline: Bexar County approves 10-year tax break for H-E-B East Side expansion
items.summary: Bexar County commissioners approved a 10-year property-tax abatement for H-E-B's East Side expansion. County officials estimate the agreement will reduce the company's county property-tax bill by more than $15 million while H-E-B has projected 720 new jobs.

items.headline: Cleveland City Council considers more than $1.1 million in emergency stadium repairs
items.summary: Cleveland City Council was set to hear legislation authorizing more than $1.1 million in emergency repairs to Huntington Bank Field. The Browns organization had already made most of the repairs and was seeking reimbursement from the city.

items.headline: HHSC hosts Rural Texas Strong public forum in Big Spring
items.summary: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission hosted a public forum in Big Spring to provide information and gather feedback on the Rural Texas Strong plan. The five-year plan is supported by approximately $1.4 billion in federal funding and will distribute assistance through six initiatives for rural communities.
items.entityName: Texas Health and Human Services Commission

items.headline: North Carolina invests in child care training to combat shortages
items.summary: The North Carolina General Assembly directed $1.5 million in one-time state-budget funding to expand free child-care worker training academies statewide. The funding also supports retention stipends for academy graduates who remain employed for at least one year.

items.headline: Public Consulting Group awarded Texas BuyBoard master service agreement
items.summary: Public Consulting Group was awarded a Texas BuyBoard master service agreement, making it an approved provider for more than 5,500 participating public entities across Texas. The agreement covers licensing, regulatory SaaS, cloud applications, cybersecurity advisory and digital-transformation services.

items.headline: New residential treatment center opens in North Texas for foster youth
items.summary: Texas opened the Terrell Center for Youth, a residential treatment facility for up to 30 foster youths ages 13 to 17 with complex behavioral-health, substance-use or developmental needs. The facility is operated by the Texas Health and Human Services Commission on the Terrell State Hospital campus.
items.entityName: Texas Health and Human Services Commission

items.headline: NCDHHS to host Spanish-language town hall on new NC Medicaid rules
items.summary: The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services announced a Spanish-language Cafecito and tele-town hall for Aug. 25 on upcoming federal and state changes to NC Medicaid. The department said the changes will affect eligibility and coverage for some noncitizens and provided preparation and resource guidance.
items.entityName: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
items.source: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks and NTT DATA target $1B in AI security sales by 2029
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks and NTT DATA signed a multiyear global alliance targeting $1 billion in joint business by the end of 2029. The agreement establishes a dedicated go-to-market model, shared engineering roadmap and early platform access, with initial offerings aimed at security operations, AI governance and related areas.

items.headline: Conduent expands AI strategy with Google Cloud eDiscovery collaboration
items.summary: Conduent said its collaboration with Google Cloud will bring Gemini models into the Viewpoint platform, initially for eDiscovery and data-breach response. The company said the integration is intended to accelerate analysis of complex datasets and extend generative AI across legal workflows.

items.headline: Phoenix renames park formerly named after César Chávez
items.summary: The City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation Board approved renaming the former César Chávez Park and community center in Laveen to Águila Park and Águila Community Center. The city said crews will remove old signage and install markers with the updated names.

items.headline: Florida CFO announces arrests after nearly $382,000 insurance-fraud scheme
items.summary: Florida’s Department of Financial Services announced the arrests of a life-insurance agent and her husband in an alleged scheme involving fraudulent policies and claims. The department said investigators identified $381,849 in losses and listed multiple fraud and theft charges against both defendants.

items.headline: No injuries reported after 10 rail cars derail in far west Bexar County
items.summary: Approximately 10 rail cars derailed near U.S. Highway 90 and Lacoste Road in far west Bexar County, according to Union Pacific. No injuries or spills were reported, while the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office provided traffic control and the cause remained under investigation.

items.headline: Nvidia denies report of China-specific LPU on its roadmap
items.summary: Nvidia denied a report that it planned to begin shipping a language-processing unit tailored for Chinese customers by year-end. A company spokesperson said Nvidia had no China-specific LPU product on its roadmap and no LPU sales in China at the time of the report.

items.headline: Cleveland councilmember requests inspections after man struck by tree branch at park
items.summary: A Cleveland councilmember requested priority tree inspections and maintenance at Impett Park after a man was hospitalized when a branch fell during a youth football practice. The report said dead and fallen limbs remained around the park.

items.headline: Worcester mayor discusses impact of off-duty police officer's murder
items.summary: Worcester Mayor Joe Petty described the effect on the city and police department after off-duty Worcester police officer Kurt Solomon was found deceased at his home. The report said the search for a suspect continued as of Aug. 20.

items.headline: HHSC reaches final-steel milestone for Panhandle State Hospital
items.summary: Texas Health and Human Services Commission said construction crews placed the final steel beam for the 75-bed Panhandle State Hospital in Amarillo. The $159 million hospital is expected to be completed in fall 2027 and serve a 26-county region.
items.entityName: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
items.source: Texas Health and Human Services Commission

items.headline: Phoenix calls for basin-wide action following Colorado River decision
items.summary: The City of Phoenix said new federal operating guidelines will reduce Arizona Colorado River deliveries beginning in 2027. It said Phoenix expects no immediate interruption to water service and is evaluating effects on its supplies and drought-management operations.

items.headline: New York State Department of Health recognizes National Immunization Awareness Month
items.summary: The Department said 16 landmarks across New York will be illuminated in purple and encouraged residents to keep recommended immunizations current, including for the back-to-school season.
items.entityName: New York State Department of Health
items.source: New York State Department of Health

items.headline: Ohio University launches public course-syllabus search
items.summary: Ohio University launched a public search for undergraduate course-syllabus information. The university said the tool supports compliance with the Advance Ohio Higher Education Act and lets users search course-syllabus information across the institution.

items.headline: TxDOT continues I-14 Central Texas Corridor routing study
items.summary: Texas Department of Transportation is studying five possible routes for the proposed I-14 Central Texas Corridor between Rogers and Huntsville. The agency has been holding public meetings and has not selected a final route or timeline.

items.headline: Governor DeSantis reappoints Jeremy Rodgers to Florida Commission on Ethics
items.summary: Governor Ron DeSantis announced the reappointment of Jeremy Rodgers to the Florida Commission on Ethics. The appointment is subject to Florida Senate confirmation.
items.source: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida

items.headline: Governor DeSantis reappoints Michael Hingst to Clay County Utility Authority
items.summary: Governor Ron DeSantis announced the reappointment of Michael Hingst to the Clay County Utility Authority.
items.source: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida

items.headline: Bexar County emergency agencies respond to south-county grass fire
items.summary: The Bexar County Sheriff’s Office and Bexar County Fire & Rescue responded to a grass fire near Hallmark Path in south Bexar County. Nearby residents were evacuated while crews worked to contain and extinguish the fire.

items.headline: Public hearing addresses competing Asheville hospital-bed proposals
items.summary: The Asheville Citizen Times reported on a public hearing involving proposals for new hospital beds. The hearing was part of North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services’ certificate-of-need process.
items.entityName: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services

items.headline: Cuyahoga County lead-abatement funding shortfall affects Cleveland remediation efforts
items.summary: Spectrum News 1 reported that Cuyahoga County left about $1.2 million of an $8 million lead-abatement grant unspent. The report said Cleveland also lost roughly $3 million in lead-remediation grant funding earlier in 2026.

items.headline: Phoenix police arrest 2 officers in connection with a violent traffic stop
items.summary: Phoenix Police said it arrested and fired officers Antonio Felix and Luis Vasquez Jr. after investigating an Aug. 5 traffic stop. The department said it is pursuing criminal charges and continuing to review whether others were involved or whether broader systemic concerns exist.

items.headline: Phoenix changes name of former Cesar Chavez Park to Aguila Park
items.summary: The City of Phoenix approved Aguila Park as the new name for the former Cesar Chavez Park and related community center after a community survey. The change follows a City Council order to remove Chavez's name from city streets and facilities.

items.headline: State agency recommended to oversee youth sports
items.summary: A special working group created by a 2024 economic-development law filed a report with the Massachusetts Legislature recommending a new independent agency to oversee youth sports. The proposed framework includes statewide licensing and standards for coaches and officials.
items.source: Lowell Sun / State House News Service

items.headline: JEA issues boil water advisory for customers in Southwest Nocatee
items.summary: JEA crews were repairing a 12-inch water-main break in southwest Nocatee that caused lower-than-normal pressure for some customers. JEA issued a precautionary boil-water advisory and told affected customers to boil water before drinking, cooking or making ice until the advisory is lifted.

items.headline: Could a diversion center reduce deaths in the Bexar County jail?
items.summary: Texas Public Radio reported that 96 people have died in the Bexar County jail since 2020 and that San Antonio and Bexar County officials are exploring a diversion and recovery center for some people accused of low-level offenses linked to behavioral-health, developmental or substance-use needs. The proposal includes a feasibility study examining capacity, operating procedures, locations and costs.

items.headline: Can't afford a hospital bill in New York? You may qualify for free or discounted care
items.summary: A USA Today Network explainer said New York hospitals must offer financial assistance to eligible patients and identified the standard financial-assistance application created by the New York State Department of Health. It also described protections and eligibility thresholds under New York's Hospital Financial Aid Law.
items.entityName: New York State Department of Health
items.source: The Journal News / USA Today Network

items.headline: Bexar County jail trash fire injures two deputies and an inmate
items.summary: A small trash fire at the Bexar County jail was extinguished after smoke spread through elevator shafts and inmates were relocated from affected areas. KENS5 reported that two deputies and an inmate received medical attention for non-life-threatening injuries; the Bexar County Fire Marshal's Office was investigating.

items.headline: Westerman turns rising energy demand into 345 new jobs in Bremen and Hebron
items.summary: JobsOhio reported that Westerman will invest $51.5 million to expand its Bremen headquarters and establish an additional manufacturing site in Hebron. The project is expected to create 345 jobs and more than $21.7 million in new annual payroll.

items.headline: New York State Department of Health alerts public to increase in measles cases
items.summary: The New York State Department of Health urged residents to ensure they are current on recommended immunizations, especially measles-mumps-rubella vaccination, while monitoring increased measles cases in rural areas. The release reported six confirmed cases in New York City and 23 outside the city, 29 statewide for the year at publication.
items.entityName: New York State Department of Health
items.source: New York State Department of Health

items.headline: Ohio Supreme Court again rejects $900M COVID checks case
items.summary: The Statehouse News Bureau reported that the Ohio Supreme Court again rejected a lawsuit seeking about $900 million in pandemic unemployment assistance, agreeing with the state that the federal program ended in 2021. The case challenges Governor Mike DeWine's authority to end the $300 weekly checks early, and the plaintiffs' attorney said he would seek reconsideration.

items.headline: Florida CFO announces arrest following vehicle-insurance fraud scheme
items.summary: Florida Department of Financial Services investigators announced the arrest of Adam Otrok after identifying 41 vehicle-insurance applications for luxury vehicles he did not own. The department said he attempted to defraud an insurer of $206,000 and obtained $44,704 in fraudulent funds.

items.headline: New hospital-bed proposals face North Carolina certificate-of-need review
items.summary: North Carolina Health News reported on a public hearing for competing proposals to add 92 hospital beds in Buncombe County, part of the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services certificate-of-need process. Mission, AdventHealth, Novant and UNC Health presented competing plans to state regulators.
items.entityName: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services

items.headline: Digital infrastructure growth drives $15 million Wieland expansion in Delaware
items.summary: JobsOhio reported that the Wieland Group will invest $15 million in a second Delaware production facility for high-performance data-center cooling equipment. The expansion is expected to create 100 jobs while the existing Delaware operation continues production.

items.headline: State Senator Bobby Hanig resigns from North Carolina General Assembly
items.summary: WITN reported that state Senator Bobby Hanig is resigning from the North Carolina General Assembly after losing a bid for the U.S. Congress. Governor Josh Stein will appoint a Republican to fill Hanig's District 1 seat.

items.headline: KDM Signs expands Cincinnati operations, creating 121 new jobs
items.summary: JobsOhio reported that KDM Signs is expanding its Cincinnati operations and establishing the city as a center of excellence for its North American operations. The project is expected to create 121 jobs and $6.1 million in new annual payroll.

items.headline: Valvoline Global Operations announces new global headquarters in Cincinnati
items.summary: JobsOhio reported that Valvoline Global Operations will establish a new global headquarters in Cincinnati, with the current location becoming the company's Americas hub. The company plans space for up to 120 employees while maintaining more than 400 jobs in Lexington, Kentucky.

items.headline: Luxorion Plastics plans $19 million facility in Northwest Ohio
items.summary: JobsOhio reported that Luxorion Plastics will invest $19 million to build a 45,000-square-foot facility in Leipsic, Putnam County. The advanced-manufacturing project is expected to create 60 new jobs as the company expands capacity for new contracts.

items.headline: John W. Danforth Company expands in Dublin, creating 80 jobs
items.summary: JobsOhio reported that John W. Danforth Company will relocate to a larger Dublin manufacturing and operations facility, creating 80 jobs and investing $850,000 in machinery and equipment. The new positions will add to 83 employees already based in Dublin.

items.headline: New York State Department of Health raises awareness about syphilis during pregnancy
items.summary: The New York State Department of Health announced the second annual Syphilis During Pregnancy Awareness Day under a proclamation from Governor Kathy Hochul. The release said the observance supports prevention, early detection and timely treatment, with state landmarks illuminated magenta and white on August 24.
items.entityName: New York State Department of Health
items.source: New York State Department of Health

items.headline: Maricopa County highlights eviction-prevention pilot in August 24 bulletin
items.summary: Maricopa County said its Eviction Prevention Pilot Program was on track to help hundreds of individuals and families stay in their homes through up to two months of rental assistance and case-management resources. The county said HOM, Inc. is administering the program and the City of Phoenix will provide utility assistance and case management.

items.headline: Bexar County detention center passes state inspection
items.summary: The Bexar County Adult Detention Center received a passing score after a two-day inspection by the Texas Commission on Jail Standards, according to the Bexar County Sheriff’s Office. The review covered operations, maintenance and inmate-care protocols.

items.headline: Boat manufacturer plans $6 million Beaufort County campus and 179 jobs
items.summary: North Carolina announced that Boater’s World Manufacturing Group plans to invest more than $6 million in a Beaufort County manufacturing campus and create 179 jobs. The release says the Governor’s Office, Department of Commerce, General Assembly and local leaders worked together to support the project.

items.headline: Governor DeSantis announces first rollout of CORE emergency-management education initiative
items.summary: Governor Ron DeSantis announced the first rollout of the Coalition for Operational Readiness in Education at Florida International University. The statewide initiative is a cross-agency partnership intended to expand hands-on emergency-management training and workforce pathways.
items.source: Office of the Governor of Florida

items.headline: Legal challenges continue over New York Climate Change Superfund Act
items.summary: A Spectrum News report said a federal judge questioned whether New York’s Climate Change Superfund Act is preempted by federal law. The report notes Governor Kathy Hochul signed the act in 2024 and that legal challenges have kept it from taking effect.

items.headline: Governor Healey celebrates new law to make medical devices safer for patients
items.summary: Governor Maura Healey highlighted a new Massachusetts law that will phase out the cancer-linked chemical DEHP from IV bags and tubing sold in the state. The release says the law is intended to make medical devices safer for patients.

items.headline: New York urges precautions after West Nile virus activity
items.summary: The New York State Department of Health urged residents to take precautions against West Nile virus and described prevention steps as mosquito activity continues. The advisory is a direct public-health action by the department.

items.headline: Ohio to receive millions from historic Meta settlement
items.summary: Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson said the state will receive $319 million over a decade from a multistate settlement with Meta and that his office will work with the Ohio General Assembly on how the funds are used.

items.headline: Luxorion plans $19 million northwest Ohio expansion with 60 new jobs
items.summary: Luxorion Plastics announced a $19 million, 45,000-square-foot facility in Putnam County expected to create 60 jobs; JobsOhio said the project is based in Leipsic.

items.summary: The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services reported 940 statewide cyclosporiasis cases as of August 26, including 11 new cases since its prior update. The report cited the state’s disease dashboard.

items.headline: Governor Healey calls for reversal of changes that would dismantle Head Start
items.summary: Governor Maura Healey joined Massachusetts education leaders, providers, teachers and families in opposing proposed federal changes they said would weaken Head Start’s early-education, safety and family supports. The governor’s release urges the administration to reverse the changes.

items.headline: Healey and congressional leaders sound alarm on Trump’s research cuts
items.summary: Governor Maura Healey and Massachusetts congressional leaders issued a statement after meeting to discuss opposition to federal research cuts, citing the importance of science and medicine to the state economy and research institutions.

items.headline: Metallus commissions furnaces supporting U.S. Army munitions production
items.summary: Metallus and the U.S. Army commissioned new furnaces and an automated sawline at the steelmaker’s Ohio plants. The report says the Army provided $99.75 million and JobsOhio provided $3.5 million for the expansion.

items.headline: Nvidia quarterly results again exceed Wall Street expectations as AI-chip revenue surges
items.summary: Nvidia reported $59.69 billion in net income and $96.22 billion in quarterly revenue, with revenue more than doubling year over year; it forecast about $108 billion for the next quarter. The company said data-center revenue reached $89 billion, reinforcing continued AI-infrastructure demand.

items.headline: Governor Stein proclaims August 26 Women’s Equality Day
items.summary: Governor Josh Stein declared August 26 Women’s Equality Day and highlighted equitable access to the ballot box and services for North Carolina women and families. The Department of Administration’s Council for Women and Division for Women and Youth joined the statewide recognition.

items.headline: Palantir CEO says AI sovereignty is the future
items.summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp argued that companies should retain control over their data and AI capabilities rather than depend on a small group of frontier AI labs. The interview presents Palantir’s AI-sovereignty strategy for government and commercial customers.

items.headline: Texas Legislature posts interim hearings for week of August 31
items.summary: The Texas Legislative Reference Library posted the Legislature’s interim-hearing schedule for the week of August 31, including House and Senate committee meetings on health care affordability, local government, water and transportation funding.

items.headline: Governor Hochul celebrates opening of the 2026 Great New York State Fair
items.summary: Governor Kathy Hochul marked the opening of the 2026 Great New York State Fair and highlighted agricultural, educational and visitor programming at the event.

items.headline: Pennsylvania governor says Eagles stadium will remain in Philadelphia
items.summary: Governor Josh Shapiro said the Eagles’ future stadium will be in Philadelphia as the team explores long-term stadium options. He said his administration will work with the franchise on the eventual plan.
